recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed unless a future publisher regression drops the fhir.ini-driven metadata or Dosage entries from the generated wildcard or extension type lists.
issue_request: FHIR-12986 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I change request for DSTU2 asking that the open type element list for '*' include the STU3 metadata datatypes and the medication-specific Dosage datatype so extensions and operation Parameters could use them.
initial_application: The Jira comment's svn revision 12844 maps to git commit 0abcdc927256a7fe25537a22cb7ca351249ee9b5, which added Dosage and the then-current metadata datatypes to the hand-maintained open type list in source/datatypes.html. Commit dcd3ffda9020726ce3628f04603b19e4bf289c52 later single-sourced the wildcard and extension lists through generated placeholders in source/datatypes.html and source/extensibility.html.
additional_context: The active current [types] list in source/fhir.ini includes ContactDetail, DataRequirement, ParameterDefinition, RelatedArtifact, TriggerDefinition, UsageContext, and Dosage, along with current successor metadata types; Contributor is absent because later model changes removed it as a datatype. The active Parameters StructureDefinition explicitly lists the issue-relevant metadata datatypes and Dosage for Parameters.parameter.value[x]. Current CI-rendered datatypes and extensibility pages show the metadata datatypes and valueDosage, and community searches found no conflicting Zulip or Confluence evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the authoritative source and rendered output already satisfy the issue request.
